targets.title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
targets.study_numbers: Figure 7C, Supplemental Figures S2A and S7C
targets.evidence_quote: As part of the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology we published a Registered Report (Fiering et al., 2015) that described how we intended to replicate selected experiments from the paper ‘Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis’ (Goetz et al., 2011). Here we report the results.
targets.outcome_quote: Primary tumor growth was similar between conditions, like the original study (Supplemental Figure S7Ca; Goetz et al., 2011). We found metastatic burden was similar between Cav1WT and Cav1KO pMEFs, while the original study found increased metastases with Cav1WT (Figure 7C; Goetz et al., 2011); however, the duration of our in vivo experiments (45 days) were much shorter than in the study by Goetz et al. (2011) (75 days). This makes it difficult to interpret the difference between the studies as it is possible that the cells required more time to manifest the difference between treatments observed by Goetz et al. We also found a statistically significant negative correlation of intratumoral remodeling with metastatic burden, while the original study found a statistically significant positive correlation (Figure 7Cd; Goetz et al., 2011), but again there were differences between the studies in terms of the duration of the metastasis studies and the imaging approaches that could have impacted the outcomes.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors report agreement for extracellular matrix contraction and null primary tumor growth, but disagreement for metastasis and the direction of the remodeling–metastasis correlation. Timing and measurement caveats do not amount to an overall uninformative verdict.

reasoning: New cell and animal experiments retest one original paper. The earlier Registered Report is the protocol, not a second target. Title, DOI and author list verified on the publisher full text.
